name: Effective Range / Radon Number (affine)
details: For every finite binary concept class, $\mathrm{Rad}(\mathcal H)\leq\mathrm E(\mathcal H)+1$.
proof: Let $R=\{h_1,\ldots,h_r\}$ be Radon independent.  The singleton-versus-rest partition for $h_i$ has disjoint convex hulls, so $h_i$ is not in the version-space convex hull of $R\setminus\{h_i\}$.  Hence some coordinate $x_i$ is constant on $R\setminus\{h_i\}$ and has the opposite value on $h_i$.  When $r\geq3$, the coordinates $x_i$ are distinct: if $x_i=x_j$, any third member of $R$ would have to equal both opposite constant values.  Every $x_i$ is active, so $r\leq\mathrm E(\mathcal H)$.  For $r\leq2$, the weaker bound $r\leq\mathrm E(\mathcal H)+1$ is immediate (two distinct concepts differ on an active coordinate).
witness_verification: For $\mathcal T_n=\{\emptyset,[n]\}$, effective range is $n$ while the Radon number is $2$; hence no reverse affine-linear bound holds.
